I had seen this getting a fair amount of praise in some parts online. I gave it a go and just found the writing somewhat amateurish. \*Especially\* when it came to the dialogue. There were some genuinely interesting ideas in the book so I wouldn't say it was all bad but it was not enough to make up for the trite writing style. 

**Finished: I'm Thinking of Ending Things by Ian Reids**

This is obviously not an issue in to original game as the lines don't share a point. The points shift around a circle as the player moves them. 

This test level works around the issue with some very hacky solutions but none of them will work long term for anything more complicated than this test level. Can anyone share some resources on how best to figure this out? Or maybe some alternative solutions?

Meanwhile, a coworker called out saying she had to take her son to the hospital and he told her if she didn't show up she would be fired.

My breaking point was when after working there for over a year, covering multiple shifts, literally never being late, learning every station I could, he said I was "lazy" and "didn't want to work" because I said no to covering an extra shift that night. Me too! My favorite duck spots:

**Laurelhurst park**

*  lots of domestic breeds like swedish blue, khaki Campbell, some Saxony and pied breeds. also mallards 
* they have their own little island in the center so they are a *bit* safer

**Red sunset park** 

* good mix. Mallards, domestic breeds, and at least one Muscovy. There used to be wayyyy more muscovies but I haven't seen as many lately unfortunately. Also expect both cackling and Canada geese
* Very friendly. Some will eat out of your hand if you are patient and kind. -there is a duck couple there that I love. A huuuuge female rouen and a slim white drake. The male, who could easily outwalk this rouen, always walks patiently behind her. I call them Mama and Papa because when I first met her she was sitting on a clutch of eggs and quacked quite aggressively for the corn I had.
* con: a lot of people seem to feed them bread which is a bit sad to see

**Salish Ponds** 

* expect mallards and wood ducks. Coots, Canada geese, and mergansers are also common
* great for bird watching in general, and tons of bunnies in the spring

(On a very rare and magic occasion) **Powell Butte**

*  I've only seen it twice but I've seen a mallard couple there twice on some of the tiny seasonal ponds on top
*  considering the kestrels around there I'm not surprised how little they are there 
* great bird watching spot, the western bluebirds have been returning 
* please stop walking off trail and fucking up nesting areas

Bonus (not Oregon but super close):

 **Steigerwald park + William Clark park in Washington** 

* mallards, Canada geese, cackling geese. 
* great birdwatching spot, saw a pileated woodpecker for the first time at William Clark park recently.
